en: The Legend of the Elder Piyālaphaladāyaka Sobhita Chapter, Number Ten I gave a piyāla fruit to the Buddha Vipassī, who was seated beneath a tree. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in the realm of the Thirty-Three Gods; there I enjoyed divine pleasures, possessing celestial splendor and majesty. When my lifespan there had come to an end, I passed away from that world and was reborn here in the human realm. In every birth, I was born into a wealthy family, possessing great wealth and vast resources. I was always handsome, fair-skinned, and possessed of great beauty. My complexion was golden, and I was endowed with all auspicious marks. I was beloved by many people, and I was honored by the multitude. I was a giver of gifts, a performer of meritorious deeds, and one who delighted in generosity. I was never poor, nor did I ever lack for food or clothing. I was always well-provided for, and I lived in comfort and ease. I was a king of kings, a sovereign ruler over the four continents. I possessed the seven treasures and the four bases of power. I ruled as a wheel-turning monarch, a lord of the earth. I governed the entire world, bringing it under my dominion. I was a universal monarch, a conqueror of the whole world. I possessed the seven jewels and the four bases of power. I was a righteous king, a protector of the world. I was a donor of alms, a performer of sacrifices, and a patron of the Sangha. I gave gifts to the Saṅgha, and I performed acts of merit. I gave alms-food to the monks, and I offered robes and bedding. I gave medicine to the sick, and I provided them with all necessities. I gave lamps and oil, and I offered incense and perfumes. I gave flowers and garlands, and I offered parasols and banners. I gave flags and streamers, and I offered various kinds of ornaments. I gave food and drink, and I provided all manner of delicacies. I gave garments and cloths, and I offered fine fabrics and silks. I gave gold and silver, and I offered precious gems and pearls. I gave coral and cat's-eye, and I offered lapis lazuli and crystal. I gave conch shells and amber, and I offered various kinds of jewels. I gave elephants and horses, and I offered chariots and palanquins. I gave villages and towns, and I offered cities and kingdoms. I gave wives and children, and I offered my own sons and daughters. I gave my head and eyes, and I offered my hands and feet. I gave my ears and nose, and I offered my flesh and blood. I gave my marrow and bones, and I offered my very life. Through such deeds, I attained this state of peace and happiness. I have now reached the final stage of existence, the end of suffering. I have seen the Buddha, the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One. I have heard the Dhamma, the teaching of the Well-Gone One. I have entered the Sangha, the community of the Noble Ones. I have taken refuge in the Triple Gem, the supreme refuge.

I have abandoned all evil, and I have cultivated all that is wholesome. I have destroyed the defilements, and I have attained liberation. I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra, and I have reached the further shore. I am now an Arhat, free from all taints, and I dwell in peace. This is the legacy of the Elder Piyālaphaladāyaka. May all beings attain such a state of peace and happiness. May they all reach the end of suffering and attain Nibbāna.
At that time I was a pigeon,
not causing any obstruction;
I made my bed upon a mountain slope.
Not far from the Teacher of the Śākya clan,
I see in the evening and at dawn the Buddha,
the supreme leader of the world.
I have no gift to offer to the Lord of Bipeds, the Tathāgata;
having taken a piyāla fruit, [I approach him].
He approached the presence of the Buddha;
the Blessed One, the eldest in the world, the bull among men, accepted it.
From that time forward,
having taken him as my attendant and guide,
through that clarity of mind,
I passed away there;
in the thirty-first aeon from now,
I gave that fruit.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving fruit.
In the fifteenth aeon from now,
There were three who were beloved;
they were wheel-turning monarchs of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Piyaḷaphaladāyaka spoke these verses.
The legend of the elder Piyaḷaphaladāyaka is the tenth.
The fourteenth chapter, the Sobhita-vagga, is concluded.
Its summary verse is: Sobhita and Sudassana,
Candana and Pupphacchadana;
Raha, Campakapupphi,
and Atthasandassaka;
Ekapasādi and Sāladada.
The tenth is the giver of fruit;
seventy-two verses have been counted by those of discerning insight.
